statuut.title: Statuut voor het Koninkrijk der Nederlanden (BWBR0002154): wijzigingshistorie
statuut.note: Version history of the Charter for the Kingdom: "29-12-1954 Nieuwe-regeling Datum inwerkingtreding: 29-12-1954 Ontstaansbron: Stb. 1954, 503 Inwerkingtredingsbron: Stb. 1954, 596". Art. 61: the Charter enters into force at its solemn proclamation after the King's confirmation (given on 15 December 1954). Arts. 41-42 and 46: the Netherlands Antilles run their own affairs under their Staatsregeling, and their representative bodies are elected by free and secret vote.

nak.title: Nederlands-Antilliaans Kiesreglement (P.B. 2001, no. 159, as amended)
nak.note: Electoral law for the Staten. Art. 13(1): a hoofdstembureau in each island territory, chaired by the gezaghebber; arts. 14 and 33: the nomination and polling days of a periodic election are set by landsbesluit, and after a dissolution by the Governor; arts. 90-91 and 99: list proportional representation by Hare quota and largest averages, and in a one-member district the seat goes to the list with most votes.

erna.title: Koninklijk Besluit van 3 maart 1951, houdende de Eilandenregeling Nederlandse Antillen
erna.note: Island regulation, version in force from 22 July 2006. Art. 5: Curaçao's island council has 21 members; art. 6: proportional representation, free and secret; art. 8: island ordinances govern the franchise and the elections; art. 16: members sit for four years; art. 16a: a one-time early dissolution of Curaçao's council; art. 106: Bonaire 9 members, Sint Maarten 11 (15 after an art. 16a dissolution), Saba and Sint Eustatius 5 each.

classes.name: Verkiezing van de leden van de Staten van de Nederlandse Antillen
classes.finest_note: Seats and votes by island district; each island's hoofdstembureau counted by polling station, but no official count by station is online.
classes.locator: https://zoek.officielebekendmakingen.nl/kst-26605-2.html (22 members elected at general elections for four years: Curaçao 14, Bonaire 3, Sint Maarten 3, Saba and Sint Eustatius 1 each)
classes.note: The unicameral legislature of the Netherlands Antilles: 22 members elected for four years by list proportional representation, each island territory forming one district. Until 1985 the districts were Curaçao (12 seats), Aruba (8), Bonaire (1), and the three Windward Islands together (1); from the election of 22 November 1985, after Aruba's departure, Curaçao 14, Bonaire 3, Sint Maarten 3, Saba 1, and Sint Eustatius 1. The polling day is set by landsbesluit, or by the Governor after a dissolution, and early elections followed dissolutions in 1958, 1969, 1979, and 1982. The Staten elected on 15 November 1954, a few weeks before the Charter took effect, sat as the country's first legislature until 1958; that election, and those of 1937 to 1949 for the Staten of Curaçao and of the Netherlands Antilles before autonomy, fall outside this span. Results were declared by each island's hoofdstembureau and printed in the Amigoe di Curaçao and the other island papers; no electoral body published them online before the dissolution.

cadence.administered_by: Hoofdstembureaus of the island territories, chaired by the gezaghebbers
cadence.locator: https://lokaleregelgeving.overheid.nl/CVDR1533/2 (art. 13(1): "In elk eilandgebied wordt voor de verkiezing van de Staten een hoofdstembureau ingesteld."; art. 33: polling day set by landsbesluit)

access.evidence: The Amigoe di Curaçao and Dutch national papers printed the island governments' notices and the seats and votes by island for each Staten election from 1958 to 1998; Antillean coverage ends about 2005

Each island's hoofdstembureau declared the count (Kiesreglement art. 13); none of their records is online, and the successor governments of Curaçao and Sint Maarten publish no historical Staten results

classes.name: Verkiezing van de leden van de eilandsraden
classes.finest_note: Seats and votes by island territory; Saba, Sint Eustatius, and Sint Maarten voted as districts of the Windward Islands territory until 1983.
classes.note: Each island territory elected its island council for four years by list proportional representation under the Eilandenregeling of 1951 and its own island ordinance: Curaçao 21 seats, Aruba 21 (until it left on 1 January 1986), Bonaire 7 then 9, and the Windward Islands territory 15 (five per island) until it was split into Sint Maarten, Saba, and Sint Eustatius on 1 April 1983; Sint Maarten's council then grew from 7 to 9, 11, and finally 15 seats, while Saba and Sint Eustatius kept 5. The islands often voted on different days, each set by its own government, so each row lists the islands that voted that day. The first island councils were elected on 4 June 1951, before the Charter took effect. Curaçao and Sint Maarten held early elections in August and September 2010 for the councils that became their first Staten; Bonaire, Saba, and Sint Eustatius held none before the dissolution, their next elections falling in 2011 as Dutch public bodies, which belong to the Netherlands' census.

classes.name: Referenda over de staatkundige toekomst van de eilandgebieden
classes.finest_note: Results by island, some by polling station in the island governments' notices.
classes.note: Consultative referendums held by the island territories on their constitutional future, each under its own island ordinance (for example Saba's ordinance for the vote of 5 November 2004, CVDR30428, and Sint Eustatius's of 2005, CVDR40046): Aruba in 1977, all five islands in 1993 and 1994, then Sint Maarten in 2000, Bonaire and Saba in 2004, Curaçao and Sint Eustatius in 2005, and Curaçao again in 2009 on the agreement that dissolved the country. The Netherlands Antilles held no country-wide referendum.

access.evidence: The Amigoe di Curaçao and Dutch national papers printed the notices and the results by island
Dutch parliamentary papers give the date, turnout, and winning option of each referendum from 2000 to 2009

dates.quote: dat de stemming voor het referendum bij wijze van opinie-peiling op vrijdag 25 maart 1977 plaatsvindt
dates.note: Aruba's consultative referendum on independence, held as an opinion poll by the island government; about 82% chose independence.

dates.quote: De bevolking van Cura?ao heeft zich in het gisteren gehouden referendum massaal — 74 procent van de uitgebrachte stemmen — uitgesproken voor handhaving van de Antilliaanse
dates.note: Curaçao's status referendum; a second round planned for 26 November was not needed.

dates.quote: Ook de beide andere Bovenwindse eilanden, Sint Eustatius en Saba, hielden vrijdag een referendum.
dates.note: Status referendums on Sint Maarten, Saba, and Sint Eustatius; each chose to stay in the Netherlands Antilles.

dates.quote: Dat was het resultaat van het vrijdag gehouden referendum over de staatkundige toekomst van Bonaire.
dates.note: Bonaire's status referendum, the last of the five islands in the 1993-1994 round.

dates.quote: Tijdens het op 23 juni 2000 op Sint Maarten gehouden raadplegend referendum
dates.note: Sint Maarten's consultative status referendum; status aparte won 68.9%.

dates.quote: Op 10 september 2004 is op Bonaire een referendum gehouden.
dates.note: Bonaire's status referendum; turnout 56.1%.

dates.quote: Op 5 november 2004 is op Saba een referendum gehouden.
dates.note: Saba's status referendum; turnout 78%.

dates.quote: Op 8 april 2005 is op Sint Eustatius een referendum gehouden.
dates.note: Status referendums on Sint Eustatius and Curaçao the same day (Curaçao: Kamerstuk 32213, nr. 45, "op Curaçao op 8 april 2005").

dates.quote: het op 15 mei 2009 gehouden referendum waarbij de meerderheid van de bevolking van Curaçao te kennen had gegeven akkoord te gaan
dates.note: Curaçao's referendum approving the round-table agreement on its new status.

classes.name: Gouverneur van de Nederlandse Antillen
classes.disposition_reason: The Governor represented the King and headed the Antillean government; the Crown appointed and dismissed him (Charter art. 2), and the ministers were appointed and answered to the Staten, so no executive was elected.

classes.name: Gezaghebbers van de eilandgebieden
classes.name_en: Lieutenant governors of the island territories
classes.disposition_reason: Each island territory's gezaghebber, who also chaired its hoofdstembureau (Kiesreglement art. 13), was appointed by the Crown, and its executive council (bestuurscollege) was chosen by the island council from among its members, so no island executive was elected.
